description: HES-SO Valais-Wallis publishes PowerData as a toolset for generating power-system time series for machine-learning and simulation studies. The repository combines a Python module for synthetic series based on historical inputs with a linked Julia temperate optimal-power-flow package. It supplies usage notebooks, a continental European grid model and examples restricted to individual countries. Coverage and duration follow the selected network and source series; the published demonstration generates hourly European profiles. Source is free on GitHub under MIT. The workflow can create load and dispatch scenarios for network simulations and exchange model data with model-powermodels-jl. A caveat is that statistical similarity to historical aggregates does not establish that every synthetic trajectory is a realised operating condition. Reproduction requires matching network, input and dispatch settings, and the Julia solver has its own dependencies. No generator, dispatch computation or notebook was executed.
